name: Knowledge-bearing repetition
summary: Repetition earns its next attempt when the previous attempt leaves a usable distinction about route, timing, enemy, resource, rule, or consequence.
player_action: The player compares the last failure with the current attempt and changes a decision.
system_response: The game preserves causal evidence and presents another opportunity to test the changed hypothesis.

conflicts_with: identical replay with no remaining decision

failure_modes: The player cannot name what to change.
A changed decision cannot be compared because unrelated variables drift.
The game records completion but not the learned distinction.
Repetition continues after every meaningful uncertainty is resolved.
accessibility: Preserve learned distinctions through optional journals and cue glossaries.
Allow repetition speed to change without silently solving the decision.

smallest_playable_test.setup: One short loop with three discoverable causal rules, an attempt log, controlled seeds, and optional hints.
smallest_playable_test.retain_if: Most failed attempts produce a testable change and mastery reduces error without exhausting all uncertainty immediately.
smallest_playable_test.revise_if: Players learn but cannot retrieve or apply the distinction after interruption.
smallest_playable_test.reject_if: Repeated attempts differ only in outcome, time, or luck and produce no actionable comparison.

evidence.claim: Supergiant describes Hades as repeated escape attempts in which story and relationships continue to unfold while the player combines changing powers.
evidence.notes: Supports repetition that carries knowledge and narrative context rather than only restarting combat.
